   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, November 15, 2022

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Menchaca,
  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. CEREMONIAL SWEARING IN OF POLICE CAPTAIN EDWIN BROCK

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-71 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-71 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions. There is no fiscal impact related
  to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-71 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 1, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  2
   Recommended Action: Approval

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE – OCTOBER 2022

  This report provides the monthly budget update for the City’s General Fund
  and Mission Playhouse as of October 31, 2022. The monthly budget
  incorporates the actual revenue received and expenditures that have occurred
  through October 31, 2022, and projects the financial results for the year ending
  on June 30, 2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 22-64 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL FIRE MANAGEMENT GROUP
  (FMG) FOR THE JULY 1, 2020 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022 PERIOD AND
  INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR FIRE MANAGEMENT
  SALARIES

  The most recent Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City and
  the San Gabriel Fire Management Group (FMG) expired on June 30, 2020.
  Representatives of the City and FMG have conferred over a successor MOU for
  the last several months and have now reached an agreement on a proposed
  two-year MOU for the period covering July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2022,
  presented for Council consideration. The successor MOU with FMG is expected
  to have a total two-year cost impact of $139,730, of which $32,826 is for Fiscal
  Year 2021-22 and $106,903 is for Fiscal Year 2022-23. An additional General
  Fund appropriation of $139,730 is needed to cover the increased cost to Fire
  Management personnel salaries for Fiscal Year 2022-23.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-64, which
  approves the two-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2020
  through June 30, 2022 between the City and FMG and increase General Fund
  appropriations of $139,730 to cover increased costs to Fire Management
  salaries.

  F. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MNS ENGINEERS,
  INCORPORATED FOR GRANT-WRITING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $41,560 FOR THE SENATE BILL 1 PARTNERSHIP COMPETITIVE PROGRAM
  FOR VALLEY BOULEVARD REVITILIZATION PROJECT

  Valley Boulevard is one of San Gabriel’s busiest arterial streets with some of the
  most deteriorated pavement in the City. The 2018 Pavement Management
  Program update found that much of Valley Boulevard is considered “very poor”
  with an average Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 20 out of 100. In April 2020,
  the City awarded a contract to MNS Engineers, Incorporated (MNS) to apply for
  an Urban Greening Grant for Valley Boulevard Streetscape and Reconstruction
  project through the California Natural Resources Agency. Although the City was
  not selected, MNS continuously seeks funding opportunities for repaving Valley
  Boulevard.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-70 to
  appropriate $41,560 from the Development Impact Fund to account 124-800-
  40-96-813; and authorize the City Manager to execute a Professional Services
  Agreement with MNS Engineers, Incorporated in the amount of $41,560 for
  grant writing services as well as approve a Purchase Order in an amount not to
  exceed $41,560 from account 124-800-40-96-813.

  G. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 22-06 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $490,000 TO HARDY & HARPER, INCORPORATED FOR COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT STREET IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT FISCAL
  YEAR 2022-2023

  Construction Contract 22-06 is primarily funded through the Los Angeles
  County Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds. The CDBG Street
  Improvements Project Fiscal Year 2022-23 is designated for eligible income
  residential areas. Padilla Street (from South Mission Drive to South Santa Anita
  Avenue), De Anza Street (from West Las Tunas Drive to South End), Marshall

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  4
   Street (from Walnut Street to California Street), Marshall Street (from California
  Street to San Gabriel Boulevard) is part of an approved list for four selected
  street local segments for this Fiscal Year 2022-23 CDBG Street Improvement
  Project. The project consists of edge grinding to a depth of 4 inches below the
  existing pavement and tapered to zero inches at a distance of 7 feet from the
  edge along selected four streets and placing a new 4 inch thick layer of asphalt
  rubber hot mix (ARHM) over the existing pavements over the entire surface for
  a total of 1 road mile of street segments, which has a pavement condition index
  (PCI) range between 24 and 36. Weed removal and crack-sealing work will be
  performed in advance of paving as necessary by City crews to project costs.
  Staff is requesting an appropriation of $101,341 from the CDBG fund to the
  CDBG Street Improvements Project account 122-800-53-97-733.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 22-73 to appropriate $101,341 from the Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) fund to account 122-800-53-97-733;
  2. Approve plans and specifications for the CDBG Street Improvements Project
  Fiscal Year 2022-2023, Contract No. 22-06;
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Hardy & Harper,
  Incorporated for the total bid amount of $490,000; and
  4. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Hardy &
  Harper, Incorporated in the amount of $539,000, which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

  H. PEDEDSTRIAN AND BICYCLE SAFETY PROGRAM – OFFICE OF TRAFFIC
  SAFETY GRANT FOR FEDERAL FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  The Police Department has received a grant from the Office of Traffic Safety
  (OTS) to participate in the Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program (STEP) for
  Federal Fiscal Year 2022-2023. The grant will reimburse the City for personnel
  overtime costs incurred to participate in this campaign and for the purchase of
  related equipment in the sum of $25,000. There will be no impact to the General
  Fund with the acceptance of the grant.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-68 approving
  and accepting the Office of Traffic Safety contract funding outlined in this Staff
  Report and increasing the Revenue Budget Account 147-3229 by an estimated
  $25,000 to reflect receipt of the grant funds and increasing the Police

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  5
   Department Expenditure Budget by $25,000, in various accounts of fund 147,
  the Office of Traffic Safety fund, which will be used for overtime costs and the
  purchase of any related equipment.

  I. SECOND AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  LISA WISE CONSULTING, INCORPORATED (LWC) FOR PREPARATION OF
  HOUSING PROGRAMS

  The Community Development Department is requesting a Second Amendment
  to an existing professional services agreement with Lisa Wise Consulting,
  Incorporated (LWC) for preparation of housing programs at a grant-funded
  additional cost of $19,300, for City Council-requested analysis. These services
  are funded by a $160,000 Senate Bill 2 Planning Grant and $150,000 LEAP Grant,
  which is paid on a reimbursement basis, but does not require matching funds.
  The deadline to use these funds is September 30, 2023.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff Recommends that the City Council approve the Second Amendment to
  the Professional Services Agreement with Lisa Wise Consulting, Incorporated
  (LWC) for an expanded scope of services in the existing Agreement for
  completion of the Inclusionary Housing and Density Bonus Analysis and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment.

  J. PURCHASE OF GRANT-FUNDED BODY ARMOR IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $20,197.80

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is purchasing new grant-funded Level IIIA
  Ballistic Body Armor for its members. As an all-risk response agency, the Fire
  Department is tasked with response to violent events including acts of terror,
  assaults, and active shooter incidents, law enforcement standby and barricade
  suspect situations. This purchase will replace out of date ballistic vests and
  enable each member to have a custom fit vest as a part of the personal
  protective package. For streamlining and quantity pricing, the Fire Department
  has adopted the same ballistic protection specifications as used by the San
  Gabriel Police Department. State Homeland Security Program (SHSP) funds in
  the amount of $20,000 from the previously accepted (Resolution No. 22-26,
  May 17, 2022) 2020 State Homeland Security Grant Program award have been
  allocated to this purchase.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  6
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize and the City Manager to issue
  a purchase order to U.S. Armor Corporation, not to exceed $20,197.80 for
  purchasing the items as detailed in the report under the City’s purchasing
  policy.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 686 – ADOPTION
  OF THE 2022 CALIFORNIA BUILDING AND FIRE CODES

  The California Building Standards Commission has adopted new building and
  fire codes to take effect on January 1, 2023. Publications were available as of July
  this year. The Building and Safety Division and Fire Department staff have
  monitored the development of these codes closely and are engaging in training
  to ensure that the City’s building and safety and fire personnel are properly
  trained to implement the new standards. There is no fiscal impact related to this
  item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 686.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. GRAPEVINE GUIDE AND GRAPEVINE NEWSLETTER MERGE

  The City of San Gabriel produces two publications, Grapevine Guide and
  Grapevine Newsletter, that are each released four times a year, for a total of
  eight publications a year. Staff is seeking Council’s approval to combine the two
  publications into one consolidated publication, develop a new name and
  updated theme, and release a request for proposal for printing and design
  services accordingly. The current budget for Fiscal Year 2022-23 is $15,000 and
  $56,000 for the Grapevine Newsletter and Grapevine Guide, respectively. The
  fiscal impact will be determined once the results of the requests for proposals
  for printing and mailing services and design services have been reviewed.
  However, merging the publications will reduce paper cost and eliminate
  duplicate postage fees. The costs for services will not likely exceed the amount

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 15, 2022  7
   that has already been allocated and approved by the City Council for Fiscal Year
  2022-23 ($71,000).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the merge of the Grapevine
  Guide and Grapevine Newsletter with a new name of “Discover San Gabriel” and
  allow staff to begin working on the process of creating a new design and
  cohesive magazine for release in Spring 2023.

  B. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – OCTOBER 2022

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The October 2022 Cash and
  Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s
  adopted 2022-23 Investment Policy. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash Investment
  Report for October 2022.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

  The regular meeting scheduled for December 6, 2022 at 6:30 p.m. has been
  cancelled and replaced with a Special Meeting to be held on December 6, 2022 at
  7:30 p.m. The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, December
  20, 2022 at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each

   meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.
